verdict.headline: AMD wins hyperscaler AI deals with OpenAI, Meta and Microsoft in landmark keynote
verdict.label: Hold — AMD hyperscaler crown confirmed at $553; WTI $90+ is the new danger line

verdict.rationale_short: AMD's Lisa Su keynote delivered the hyperscaler demand confirmation the AI trade required: OpenAI + Meta committed 12GW of AMD accelerator capacity, with Microsoft Azure and Oracle named as early Helios rack customers at $5-5.5M/rack. All four major hyperscalers are now AMD Helios customers — the most significant demand confirmation of the AI infrastructure cycle. But GOOGL's -4% premarket reaction to $195-205B capex guidance (FCF -$5.9B) and TSLA's gross-margin miss at 16.8% vs. 19.5% consensus drag the Magnificent Seven complex. WTI at $90.14 — the highest level of the US-Iran conflict phase — on Trump's bridge/power-plant ultimatum is the new macro danger line. VIX improvement to 16.64 (below the 17 formal trigger) reduces the regime to 4/7 breached from 5/7, but WTI at $90+ makes August CPI the most adverse oil-shock setup of the cycle entering next week's FOMC.

trade_setups.thesis: Lisa Su's keynote delivered the definitive hyperscaler demand confirmation: OpenAI + Meta = 12GW of AMD accelerator capacity; MSFT Azure and Oracle named early Helios rack customers at $5-5.5M/rack. All four major hyperscalers are now AMD Helios customers. The addressable market for Helios racks is now validated with real named-customer demand signals at commercial pricing. AMD at ~$553 is pricing in the keynote confirmation but not the full competitive re-rating vs. NVDA that will only be quantified at Nvidia's Aug 26 earnings.
trade_setups.entry: Long at $553 or on pullback to $530-540. Stop $510 (below Day 1 pre-keynote intraday low). Target $600 on first Helios volume-order announcements; $650+ on Nvidia Aug 26 confirming AMD share loss.

bear_case: Counter-thesis: WTI at $90.14 is the highest print of the US-Iran conflict phase, and Trump's 'bomb one bridge/power plant per Hormuz attack' posture removes the de-escalation safety valve that markets have counted on since the ceasefire frayed in early July. At $90+ WTI, August CPI oil pass-through becomes a near-certainty within a single FOMC meeting cycle; September hike probability at ~71% means the market is pricing a rate-hike path into an already-stressed consumer (TSLA gross margin at 1.4% operating margin on record deliveries). GOOGL's FCF turning negative (-$5.9B) on $44.9B capex in a single quarter marks the first sign AI infrastructure spending is outrunning cash generation; $195-205B full-year capex guidance implies the market had materially underestimated 2026 AI burn rates. AMD's hyperscaler wins (12GW, Helios at $5.5M/rack) are the strongest bull argument in the market today, but they translate to cash flows 18-24 months out; WTI at $90 is hitting cost structures and consumer spending in real time. If INTC misses AH tonight and guides to underwhelming 18A yields, the AI infrastructure thesis faces a dual credibility test: hyperscaler capex commitments are real (GOOGL, AMD wins), but foundry execution and end-demand returns remain unproven. Bear case trigger: WTI closes above $93 (where OPEC historically signals supply-response failure), OR INTC 18A yields land materially below expectations with no second major hyperscaler foundry win named, OR VIX re-breaches 17 with WTI above $90 simultaneously. Any two of these three triggers warrants moving to step_aside.
